summary: Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Oberlin College, Harvard under Alfred North Whitehead, and with Rudolf Carnap. He spent most of his career at Harvard (1933–1978), holding the Edgar Pierce Chair of Philosophy.

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and at the University of Hamburg. He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and taught at Heidelberg University from approximately 1973 to 1993.

Willem Caland was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University, studying under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He served as Lektor (1903) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1930) at Utrecht University.

Willem Frederik Stutterheim worked in archaeology and Indology after studying at Utrecht and completing his Ph.D. at Leiden under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He directed Surakarta College (1926–1936) and the Dinas Purbakala (1937).

Willem Lodewijk van Helten was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University, studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later served as Professor of Dutch language, literature, and Old Frisian at the University of Groningen (1882–1911).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University from around 1970 to 1983, later holding posts at Leiden University around 1983 and at the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and Joe Bransford Wilson, later teaching at Virginia, the Dharma Drum Institute, and the Chung-Hwa Institute.

William Abbott Oldfather was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Hanover College, Harvard University, and the University of Munich. He held faculty posts at Northwestern University (1903–1909) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1909–1945).
William Austin Montriou worked in Indology and law. He served as an advocate at the Calcutta High Court and was appointed Professor of Law and Jurisprudence at Presidency University around 1855.

William Blackstone was a legal scholar who was educated at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford. He later held an academic appointment at the University of Oxford from around 1758 to 1766.
William Bright was a linguist and Indologist who studied at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at UCLA (1959–1988) and the University of Colorado Boulder (circa 1989–2006).

William C. Kirby is a historian and sinologist. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn, later serving as professor and dean at Washington University in St. Louis (1980–1992) and as dean and center director at Harvard.

William Carey was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He served as Professor of Sanscrit at Fort William College (1801–1830) and was principal of Serampore College (1818–1832), which he founded.

William Carlson Smith was an Indologist and sociologist who completed degrees at Grand Island College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Southern California. Between 1912 and 1915, he conducted educational work for the American Baptist Missionary Union.

William Chambers was an Indologist and East India Company political servant (circa 1765–1793). He also served as an interpreter for the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1775–1792) and was a member of The Asiatic Society.
William Charles Macready was an Indologist who studied at Christ Church and the East India Company College. In 1854, he served in the Ceylon Civil Service as an Assistant Government Agent.

William Chittick is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Tehran. He held positions at Sharif University of Technology, SUNY Albany, and Stony Brook University.

William Doderet was an Indologist and linguist who completed his M.A. at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1880. He later served as the University Teacher of Marathi at the University of Cambridge from 1910 to 1919.

William Douglas Penneck Hill was an Indologist who studied as a scholar at King's College, Cambridge. He served as an Assistant Master at Eton College (circa 1908–1944) and as Principal of Jay Narayan Inter College.

William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, Albrecht Weber, and Rudolf von Roth. He spent his career at Yale University (1853–1894), serving as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology.
